correctness.rationale: Normalized threshold creation strings classify connected unlabeled graph types uniquely. Direct graph-neighborhood derivations give the twin-run maximum and the final leaf-run tuft identity. The first/middle/last run factorization proves H_(S,T) as a formal series including the single-run boundary. Fibonacci and dyadic formulas follow exactly; a block and union-bound proof shows the logarithmic sibling maximum and total-variation limit. A direct 4094-graph checker independently recovers graph statistics, and all 539 bounded-rational cases through order 13 match; these finite tests do not substitute for the all-order proof.

evidence: Fürnsinn–Gangl–Rubey Theorems 1 and 3 establish joint symmetry for all connected unlabeled graphs and individually for reduction classes; Theorem 30 gives a connected chordal corollary.
Their arXiv full text (v2 Oct 2026) has no occurrences of threshold and does not enumerate the subfamily.
Galvin–Wesley–Zacovic (JIS 25, 2022) counts labeled graphs by vertices, components, and dominating vertices.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The chordal-class symmetry is an aggregate identity and does not imply a same-statistic identity within a strict threshold subclass. Indeed the subclass violates it at n=4. The general graph species equations do not state or directly specialize to the formula without the new threshold run restrictions; no stronger source was found.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Known graph-wide symmetry and threshold-word uniqueness are inputs to motivation and proof, respectively; the all-order rational decomposition, explicit failure at every n>=4 and TV limit 1 are additional outcomes rather than corollaries of the existing symmetry claim.

evidence: The 2025/2026 symmetry paper defines sibling as largest closed-neighborhood class minus one and tuft as largest leaf-neighbor count (arXiv:2505.03665, Introduction).
Sciriha–Farrugia (doi:10.5402/2011/108509, Section 5) gives threshold duplicate/coduplicate structure, not a bounded two-statistic enumerator.
On threshold words the s=0 count equals F_(n-2) whereas t=0 equals 2^(n-3), already different at n=4.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Aliases include point-distinguishing for s=0, leafless for t=0, coduplicates/true twins for siblings, and normalized threshold creation strings for graph types. The positive formulas in prior structure results do not entail the joint rational H_(S,T) or asymptotic TV separation. The two zero-class formulas immediately distinguish the marginal laws within this subclass.

originality.rationale: An explicit all-order rational joint enumerator and asymptotically maximal marginal separation on connected threshold graph types are not covered by the inspected 2025/2026 general/chordal sibling-tuft equidistribution result or prior structural threshold-graph classifications. The general symmetry demonstrably fails to transfer to this strict hereditary subclass; failure itself plus full law supplies new information. Search coverage cannot establish absolute novelty.
residual_risks: Older unindexed threshold-graph run-enumeration or point-distinguishing literature may contain one marginal or a stronger equivalent formulation.
The full Galvin–Wesley–Zacovic article and full texts of nearby indexed findings were not material-read; abstract and indexed mathematical statements alone do not establish full-document noncoverage.
No independent external priority review has been completed.

value.rationale: The recent sibling–tuft theorem asserts a surprising joint symmetry on the broad connected and chordal classes; threshold graphs are a canonical, highly structured hereditary chordal subfamily in which survival is naturally testable. The result proves a robust negative boundary rather than a tiny isolated counterexample: complete bounded joint rational enumeration, exact two distinct marginal families, exact tuft moments, and an asymptotically maximal total-variation separation. These coefficients can support future searches for precisely which graph subclasses retain the global symmetry.
